title: Optimal GHZ extraction from MABK violations
abstract: We determine the least Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) extractability compatible with a Mermin-Ardehali-Belinskii-Klyshko (MABK) Bell score for every number of parties greater than two. Extractability is the largest squared overlap with a GHZ state obtainable by separate local quantum channels. Between the biseparable bound and the quantum maximum, the exact minimum is the affine interpolation from one half to one. The bound holds for normal states on tensor products of arbitrary local dimension and arbitrary binary measurements. We settle the previously unresolved range of six or more parties with an analytic proof that is uniform from four parties onward. We also determine the exact minimum when every local system is a qubit, and show that it lies strictly above the unrestricted bound at every interior score. One qutrit and qubits at all remaining parties attain every point of the bound with measurements fixed as the score varies. For at least four parties and strict interior scores, we classify all states attaining the bound with the minimum product of local support dimensions. For at least four parties on one qutrit and qubits elsewhere, we also prove that, when the extractability excess above the affine minimum is small, the trace-norm distance from the attaining mixture, up to local unitaries, is bounded by a constant times the square root of that excess. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal, and the constants are independent of the number of parties on every fixed interior interval of normalized scores.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes the precise minimum amount of GHZ entanglement that can be extracted from a quantum state given a measured violation of a MABK Bell inequality. It provides uniform analytic proofs for $n \ge 4$ parties and analyzes the stability of this bound using trace-norm distance estimates. The work is crucial for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum correlations in multipartite systems.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimum Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) extractability compatible with a given Mermin-Ardehali-Belinskii-Klyshko (MABK) Bell score for $n>2$ parties.
main_result: The exact minimum extractability is found to be $1 + t^2$, where $t$ parameterizes the deviation from the biseparable bound, and the authors provide uniform analytic proofs for $n \ge 4$ parties.
method: The analysis uses operator inequalities, Jordan's lemma to reduce verification to qubit sectors, and spectral analysis to establish lower bounds on the target overlap based on the measured Bell score.
model_or_system: The study concerns multipartite entangled quantum states, specifically testing entanglement using MABK Bell inequalities on systems of $n$ parties, which can be qubits or qutrits.
key_observables: GHZ extractability ($\Xi_n(ho)$), MABK Bell Score ($ eta$), and the normalized score parameter $t$.
important_parameters: The number of parties ($n \ge 3$), the local dimension of the Hilbert space, and the small error parameter $\epsilon$ used in stability analysis.
main_assumptions: The results hold for normal states on tensor products of arbitrary local dimension and arbitrary binary measurements; stability bounds rely on smallness conditions for the excess error $\epsilon$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general affine minimum bound using operator inequalities, then generalizing this proof to higher numbers of parties ($n \ge 4$), and finally analyzing structural questions like the stability of the bound using trace-norm distance estimates.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical determination of entanglement measures based on Bell inequalities provides fundamental tools for quantifying quantum correlations, which is central to quantum information theory.
